title: Relevance of a Junta Restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube $\\{−1,1\\}^n$, let $P\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ be a set of fixed coordinates, and fix signs on $P$. Reindex the restriction of $f$ to the remaining coordinates as a function on a sign cube of dimension equal to the number of remaining coordinates. If this reindexed function has positive influence in coordinate $i$, then the restricted function depends on the corresponding free coordinate: there are two assignments to the free coordinates that differ only there and on which the restricted function takes different values.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Positive influence of the reindexed restriction at $i$
